segments.text: Nine hectares. 38 independent houses.
And only 4% of the land built on. Everything else is a working farm.
Vegetable garden, orchard, animals, pinewood, stitched together by wooden
boardwalks. If you arrived a week ago or three years ago, you probably know this.
What this module asks of you is different.
Stop seeing five units and start seeing one single house, because that is how the
guest sees it. Craveral belongs to the Belong family of brands, and Belong's
signature is giving shape to meaning.
Behind it sits a simple and demanding idea: a place that is well cared for
cares for the people in it. That is why we exist.
Not to run a hotel with a pretty garden next door.
We exist to regenerate this territory through circular economy, and we use
hospitality because it is the strongest economic and cultural engine we have
to prove it. Circular economy here is not a slogan.
It is a chain you can walk in five minutes.
The garden gives more than 70% of what the kitchen serves.
What the kitchen does not use goes to compost. The compost goes back to the garden.
What we cannot grow, we buy in the shortest radius possible: cheeses from the
region, fish from this coast, wines from the Alentejo and the Vicentina, and the
São Teotónio Laundry washes our linen and the village's.
Our back of house is itself a service to our neighbors.
We run five units: the accommodation, the farm table, Bar da Praia do Carvalhal,
the beach bar, the shop, and the São Teotónio Laundry.
Five teams, five routines, five heads.
But guests are not buying five things. They're buying Craveral.
And when the shop holds one standard and the restaurant another, they do not think
the shop is worse. They think Craveral is inconsistent.
Consistency across units is not a management detail. It is the promise.
And the house is bigger than the farm.
There is the beach bar, minutes from here, on the sand of the Costa Vicentina.
There is a Mesa do Campo. In Lisbon, at the modern art center of the Calouste
Gulbenkian Foundation, the cooking of this territory is served at a city table
inside a museum. There are the weddings, the retreats, the companies that
come here to think. Different stages, the same play.
And when you recommend something of ours, you are not selling.
You are taking the guest to more of what they already chose.
There is a part of this we say too little, and it is worth saying.
Regeneration here has to work as a business, or it is not regeneration.
It is charity in disguise. We have commitments to the house owners, to our
suppliers, to the team, and to this land.
Meeting them is not the opposite of purpose. It is the condition for it.
That is why waste bothers us so much.
Food, water, energy, time, talent, or goodwill, we waste
nothing. Because everything wasted is regeneration we can no longer pay for.
If all this works, the guest feels six things: welcomed, recognized as a
person, not processed as a booking; slowed down, with permission to do less;
cared for, without ceremony; connected to the land, the food, the people,
the village, and whoever came with them; restored, they leave lighter than they
arrived; and trusted, free to decide how they use their time here.
Those six words are your job description, whatever your role.
You leave with one question for whenever you are unsure whether something is
Craveral or not.
It is this: does this bring the person who eats closer to the person who grows?
If it does, it is ours. If it does not, it is not, however
profitable it looks. That holds for an investment decision, and it holds for how
you answer a guest on the boardwalk.
In the next modules, we go to each unit, one by one, and to the standard each one
has to hold. Stay. Belong.
